purpose: A fixed acceptance set for the EF context runtimes. Every entry was verified against its upstream source before inclusion; every reward figure is quoted from published per-task results, not estimated.
designRules: Use mature benchmarks as the grader. EF does not author tasks or graders for the acceptance set.
Three lanes test three different claims: sustained long work, interaction state, memory pressure. They are never pooled into one score.
Selection is conditioned on the ROUTE MODEL's own reward band, not on the cross-model mean. A task that is discriminating for a weak model may be saturated for ours.
Headline metrics are the benchmark's own (LHTB reward, tau2 DB x COMMUNICATE, LME-V2 accuracy). EF telemetry is reported alongside, never substituted.
A task is excluded when its published reward is saturated (>0.85) or floored (<0.15) FOR OUR ROUTE, because such a task cannot separate the arms.

route.note: The model this workspace's live suites already run. All band judgements below use the published 'DeepSeek V4 Flash' rows.

longwork.grader: hidden rebuild-from-artifact verifier; continuous partial reward in [0,1]; solved at R>=0.95
longwork.whyThisLane: The only lane that measures sustained work over hundreds of steps, which is the claim EF exists to make.
longwork.hostFeasibility: BLOCKED for parallel runs: every cited task requests 4-8 GB RAM and WSL is capped at 8 GB total, so at most one cell can run at a time.

cells.efDiscrimination: Four gated stages (smoke -> exact -> 2x QPS -> 5x QPS) with a recall floor and a required JOURNAL, so earlier performance/correctness trade-offs must survive to the end.
Five sequential stages recovering hidden config semantics; each revision fixes an old lie and may plant a new one, so resolved facts must be retained and superseded correctly.
Ten gated stages across a multi-bug RV32 core where symptoms alias; a mode that resurrects a retired root cause repeats work.
cells.anchorReason: 0.88 is above the 0.85 discriminator band for our route, so this task is NOT admitted as a discriminator. It is kept as a STABILITY ANCHOR only: a task our route usually solves, where a mode that breaks long-horizon behaviour would show a visible regression. It cannot show an improvement.

cells.efDiscrimination: A bounded rebuild budget (<=8) with a hard correctness gate then a speedup target, so profiling conclusions and regression history must persist.
cells.exclusionReason: Our route's published reward is 1.00. A saturated task cannot separate the arms, so including it would only add cost and false confidence.

excluded.reason: floored across all models; no headroom

stressExtension.note: rebuild three libraries from spec; specification retention
FLOORED for our route: 0.00. Do not use as a discriminator without a stronger route.

interaction.grader: final database state + communication criteria; pass^k over k repeated runs
interaction.whyThisLane: Native multi-turn reliability. pass^k answers 'did it work every time' rather than 'did it work once', which is the variance problem the custom suite could not resolve.
interaction.hostFeasibility: FEASIBLE: text-mode needs Python >=3.12 and uv only, no Docker and no GPU. This is the only lane that can run at scale on this host.
interaction.note: The six cited ids were confirmed present in the Verified fork, not only in upstream. The Verified fork exists because upstream tasks had policy, DB, and expected-action inconsistencies.

cells.efDiscrimination: Multi-level supersession: swap bottle+lamp, then only the lamp, then a further revision.
Conditional intent tree: return, then exchange same model, then a specific variant if out of stock.
Late intent injection plus product-id/item-id confusion; highest action count in the set.
Partial rollback: change address and all orders, then revert only the user address.
Delayed information (reservation id withheld for two rounds) then a conditional fallback.
Cross-object, cross-time current-state consistency over duplicate flights.

interaction.metric: pass^1, pass^2, pass^4 at k=4 repeats per arm

memory.grader: official question accuracy plus query latency
memory.whyThisLane: Directly measures whether long histories are retained, updated, and correctly abstained on. This is the closest published analogue to EF's own claim.
memory.hostFeasibility: BLOCKED on this host: the harness expects local Qwen3.5-9B reader and Qwen3-Embedding-8B endpoints. The GPU has 8 GB, which is below a 9B reader plus an 8B embedder. Data is 7.1 GB, of which trajectories.jsonl is 1.2 GB and screenshot bundles are 5.9 GB.
memory.storagePlan: The 5.9 GB screenshot bundles are optional for the text-only questions below; downloading trajectories.jsonl plus haystacks is ~1.2 GB.

cells.efDiscrimination: Current filter behaviour after state changed over time.
Negative knowledge: the correct answer is that a field does NOT exist. A mode that hallucinates from a folded summary fails here.
Environment-specific trap that must be learned from a past failure.
Search syntax that the environment does not support.

memory.metric: accuracy at small and medium haystack, reported with the small->medium degradation per arm

notSelected.SWE-bench Pro V2: Real (scaleapi/SWE-bench_Pro-os, v2/ with 642 tasks and a HARD-51 subset) and a sound coding grader, but it needs Docker and a long agent budget. Deferred until the LHTB lane is unblocked, since the two overlap in what they measure.
notSelected.AgencyBench V2: Real (GAIR-NLP/AgencyBench, 32 scenarios / 138 tasks, ~1M tokens and ~90 tool calls per run). Deferred as a final stress test: it is the most expensive lane and depends on a Docker sandbox.

costDiscipline.rule: Quality and reliability runs may be parallel. Any run whose purpose is realized cost must be cache-isolated (concurrency 1), because concurrent cells share a provider prefix cache.
costDiscipline.enforcement: eval/real-task/parallel.ts throws when purpose='cost' is combined with concurrency>1.
